transcript.content: Hi, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. I'm coming in today because I've been struggling with constant, uncontrollable worry and anxiety for about two years now. It feels like I'm always worrying about something, and I just can't seem to make it stop.
You mentioned worrying for about two years—has this happened on most days, and have you found it hard to control the worrying?

Yes, it honestly happens almost every single day, and it is just exhausting. I try my absolute best to distract myself or force myself to stop, but I find it incredibly difficult to control or shut it off.

{
  "category": "differential point",
  "subcategory": "physical symptoms",
  "question": "Do you also experience restlessness, fatigue, trouble concentrating, irritability, muscle tension, or sleep problems along with the worry?"

Yes, I experience severe muscle tension, especially stiff, knotted shoulders and a tight jaw, which leaves my whole body feeling achy and easily fatigued. I don't really have issues with restlessness, irritability, or trouble sleeping, though. It's mostly just this constant, painful physical stiffness that I can't seem to shake.

{
  "category": "symptom duration",
  "subcategory": "muscle tension",
  "question": "How long have you been experiencing this muscle tension and physical stiffness—has it been most days for at least six months?"

Yes, I've actually been experiencing this stiffness and muscle tension for about two years now, on most days. It has been going on much longer than six months, and it feels like my body is just constantly locked up and unable to relax.

{
  "category": "functional impairment",
  "subcategory": "daily functioning",
  "question": "How much is this worry and muscle tension affecting your daily life, such as work, relationships, or activities you enjoy?"

It affects my daily life a lot because the worries constantly intrude and disrupt my focus, whether I'm at work or with family. This anxiety spreads to every area of my life, including my finances, making it incredibly hard to function normally or ever truly relax.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates included only Generalized Anxiety Disorder, and the patient's symptoms continue to align strongly with this diagnosis. The patient reports persistent and excessive worry occurring on most days for over two years, difficulty controlling the worry, and associated physical symptoms of muscle tension and fatigue lasting for at least six months—all core diagnostic criteria for Generalized Anxiety Disorder. The absence of restlessness, irritability, and sleep disturbances does not rule out GAD, as only one of these symptoms is required. The significant functional impairment across multiple domains further supports this diagnosis. No new symptoms suggesting an alternative diagnosis (e.g., mood episodes, trauma history, obsessions, or psychosis) have emerged. Therefore, the candidate list remains unchanged.
